newsitem.title: POLAND: Swarzedz to seek trading firm, investors.
newsitem.headline: Swarzedz to seek trading firm, investors.

text.p: Polish furniture maker Swarzedz SA, currently undergoing debt restructuring, seeks to form a separate trading firm for which it would find a strategic and financial investor, the company's president said on Tuesday.

Julian Nuckowski told a meeting of analysts and journalists that the forming of the separate trading firm would ensue after the current restructuring in which about half the firm's debts would be covered by its planned issue of 3.125 million shares.

"Swarzedz is looking for an investor for itself -- for the production firm -- and for the (planned) trade network," Nuckowski told Reuters after the meeting, but would not say who the potential investors might be, whether foreign or domestic.
Swarzedz plans to issue the 3.125 million shares to creditors in the third quarter and to offer another 3.5 million shares in a one-for-one rights issue.
Nuckowski said the firm was also mulling selling a 10- percent stake later this year to a strategic investor to help with production.
He said the trading firm would also need a financial investor, adding that new share issues for the financial investor and trade investor were conceivable next year.
He said the trading firm, of which Swarzedz could own about a third, could be listed sometime in the future.
Nuckowski said Swarzedz would seek to allot shares to trade partners should the rights issue not be fully taken up.
But he said interest in the rights issue could prove significant after the firm's April financial data in which sales are seen up about 30 percent.
Swarzedz has said it expects to raise sales this year to 170.9 million zlotys from 106.9 million last year and that it could break even this year before making profits in 1998.
Last year Swarzedz lost 39.5 million zlotys.
Nuckowski said financial costs were seen rising to 19 million zlotys this year from 16 million last year before falling to 10.5 million next year and 7.7 million in 1999.
He also said the firm expected to sign trade contracts in May but would give no details.

Nuckowski also said the operating yield of its 200 million mark contract with Germany's International Moebelhandelskantor Gmbh & Co KH (IMK) signed late last year was 10 percent. The German firm is a part of Schieder Group.
